thread.title: Stocks Trim Gains; Apple Expands, P&G Lifts Dow Jones | Investor's Business Daily

author: ALAN R. ELLIOTT
title: Stocks Trim Gains; Apple Expands, P&G Lifts Dow Jones | Investor's Business Daily
text:
Stocks pulled back from early gains Thursday, as Procter & Gamble ( PG ) led the Dow Jones industrial average following a fresh dose of positive trade news.
X New Age Beverages ( NBEV ) leapt in early trade, linked to regulatory changes included in the 2018 Farm Bill. General Electric ( GE ) spiked after JPMorgan turned positive on the stock. Fiber-optic gear maker Ciena ( CIEN ) blasted past a buy point after reporting accelerating earnings growth . China stocks were off to a busy start. Amazon.com ( AMZN ) led early gains among the FANG stock tech giants, and Apple ( AAPL ) edged higher after announcing a $1 billion expansion of its campus in Austin, Texas.
The Nasdaq Composite opened to a 0.5% gain, then trimmed that to less than 0.1%. Shire ( SHPG ) and Nvidia ( NVDA ) made the strongest moves among Nasdaq 100 names.
The Dow Jones industrial average pared its advance to 0.2%, and the S&P 500 defended a 0.1% gain. General Electric soared to the top of the S&P 500. Monster Beverage ( MNST ) fell hardest among both S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 stocks.

Please contact customer service CLOSE Nasdaq Goes For Four The Nasdaq will get some spotlight today as it fights to add a fourth day to this week's rally. The Dow Jones industrial average, S&P 500 and the Nasdaq all faltered in late trade Wednesday. That left the Nasdaq still up 1.9% for the week and 3.9% above a Nov. 20 low. The index remains down 3.2% for December, and a full 3% below its 50-day moving average.
Soy Rally Lifts China Markets; Europe's Rally Fades Another glimpse of U.S.-China trade progress came in the form of legumes, with the U.S. Soybean Export Council reporting that China had bought 1.5 billion to 2 billion metric tons of soybeans. The purchases were made in the 24 hours through late Wednesday, with shipments expected to occur in the first quarter. Bloomberg described the move as "a major gesture by China toward easing tensions" in the trade war launched by the White House in its effort to restructure the rules of U.S.-China trade.
Soybean futures traded lower early Thursday, up almost 15% from a September low, and still more than 13% below their high, set in March — before tariffs were broadened against both Chinese and U.S. imports. China imposed a 25% duty on soy.
China's stock markets pulsed higher, sending both the Shanghai Composite and Hong Kong's Hang Seng index up more than 1%. That was enough to lift the Shanghai benchmark back above its 50-day moving average, and nearly 8% off its Oct. 19 low. In Japan, Tokyo's Nikkei 225 jumped 1%.
Europe's markets rallied early, after Theresa May earned a supporting vote from Parliament. But early gains withered into mixed afternoon trade: Frankfurt's DAX traded 0.2% higher, while the CAC-40 in Paris added 0.1% and London's FTSE 100 dipped 0.1%.
Dow Jones: Apple Announces Multi-City Expansion Among Dow Jones stocks, Apple advanced 0.8%. Piper Jaffray lowered Apple's price target to 222, from 250. The iPhone maker announced early Thursday it would spend $1 billion to add a new campus in Austin. Plans also included new Apple facilities in Seattle, San Diego and Culver City, Calif., as well as expansion of existing operations in Pittsburgh, New York and Boulder, Colo.
Apple stock is working to craft a bottom in a two-month consolidation.
Stocks: Ciena, New Age, GE Post Big Gains Ciena rocketed 12% higher after reporting a 66% gain in earnings and a 21% revenue advance in its fiscal fourth quarter. Both numbers swept past analyst estimates, and management announced a $500 million share buyback initiative. The gain sent the stock beyond buy range above a buy point at 32.43.
New Age Beverages skittered ahead 8% as the 2018 Farm Bill, now approved by both houses of Congress, prepares to head to the White House for a final signature. The bill includes language legalizing hemp as a crop and removing it from Schedule 1 of the Controlled Substances Act. New Age trades below 10, but was up 28% for the week on Wednesday, and climbing the right side of a possible cup base.
Among other cannabis stocks, Tilray ( TLRY ) gained 1.1%, Cronos Group ( CRON ) slipped 2.5%, and Canopy Growth ( CGC ) added 0.3%.
General Electric vaulted ahead 9% after announcing it would launch a $1.2 billion company to focus on internet-of-things applications. The move spurred JPMorgan to upgrade the stock to neutral, from underweight, and removed the stock from its short target list. GE also said it would divest its stake in cloud-based software developer ServiceMax. GE shares have dived for eight straight weeks, and are down 51% since October.
